transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this meeting to get final desk updates from each of you before I make my approval decision on the early-payment discount program. As you know, the proposal is to pay participating suppliers 30 days before invoice maturity in exchange for a 2% discount, funded from operating cash and reviewed quarterly. I'd like to go around the table -- risk, accounts payable, tax, and legal -- please share any final concerns or sign-offs so I can make an informed decision.

transcript.text: Elena, before you approve, I need to flag a risk constraint. I completed the program exposure review this morning and found that our internal working-capital policy permits no more than $1,500,000 of eligible early-payment invoices from any one supplier. The current proposal allows all approved suppliers to participate with no single-supplier cap, which would conflict with this policy limit. We'll need to incorporate a per-supplier cap of $1,500,000 into the program terms to stay compliant.

We need to incorporate this requirement into the program terms before approval, as it affects the net economics of the discount for cross-border suppliers and creates a compliance timing obligation.
